q: difference between exists and in in sql
when to use exists instead of in
sql exists or in which is faster
a:
Here's the difference between EXISTS and IN in SQL:

```sql
-- IN: compare a value against a list of values
SELECT * FROM orders
WHERE customer_id IN (SELECT id FROM customers WHERE active = 1);

-- EXISTS: test whether any matching row exists
SELECT * FROM orders o
WHERE EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM customers c
    WHERE c.id = o.customer_id AND c.active = 1
);
```

IN evaluates the subquery once and compares values; EXISTS checks rows one at a time and short-circuits as soon as a match is found. For large subqueries or NULL-prone data, EXISTS is usually faster and behaves more predictably (IN with NULLs in the list returns no matches). Use IN for small, fixed lists of values ('A', 'B', 'C').
